request.prompt:
Job T02: usp_load_dim_policy (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T02_usp_load_dim_policy.sql (SHA-256 a9565f4f944b98bb52293b124a852c693d5fad0c7accb5793a9499945f0e2b0f).
Policy dimension with type-2 history, loaded once per policy snapshot.
Invocations, in order: batch 1: SnapshotDate=2025-06-30; batch 2: SnapshotDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_policy
  Purpose  : Policy dimension for finance, actuarial and broker reporting. One
             row per version of a policy term, with its product, broker and
             customer segment. A new version starts whenever the status,
             broker, annual premium or vehicle registration changes from one
             policy snapshot to the next (type 2 history).
  Run by   : POL_SNAPSHOT_LOAD, once per policy snapshot, oldest first:
             EXEC dw.usp_load_dim_policy @SnapshotDate = '<snapshot date>'
  Output   : dw.dim_policy. Keeps history, so the procedure never truncates
             it. Deploying this script recreates the table empty: reload every
             snapshot in date order afterwards.
  Author   : MOB

  Change log
    2014-02-10  MOB   Initial version, one row per policy (CR-0655)
    2015-06-22  MOB   Broker name from the broker register (CR-0790)
    2016-09-05  TF    Direct business reported as broker DIRECT-SALES (CR-0961)
    2017-03-13  TF    Type 2 history with MERGE, surrogate key policy_sk
                      (CR-1077)
    2018-10-01  PH    Vehicle registration tracked for motor (CR-1388)
    2019-07-15  PH    Customer segment from dw.dim_customer (CR-1610)
    2020-02-03  TF    Refuse a snapshot older than the last one loaded
                      (INC-2105)
    2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_policy', N'U') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE dw.dim_policy;

CREATE TABLE dw.dim_policy (
    policy_sk             INT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
    policy_id             INT            NOT NULL,
    policy_number         VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL,
    customer_id           INT            NOT NULL,
    customer_segment      CHAR(4)        NULL,
    product_code          VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
    product_name          NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
    lob_code              VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
    broker_code           VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
    broker_name           NVARCHAR(80)   NULL,
    status                VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
    inception_date        DATE           NOT NULL,
    expiry_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
    cancellation_date     DATE           NULL,
    annual_premium        DECIMAL(12,2)  NOT NULL,
    currency              CHAR(3)        NOT NULL,
    vehicle_reg           VARCHAR(12)    NULL,
    ncd_years             INT            NULL,
    valid_from            DATE           NOT NULL,
    valid_to              DATE           NOT NULL,   -- 9999-12-31 while current
    is_current            CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,   -- Y / N
    source_snapshot_date  DATE           NOT NULL,
    load_ts               DATETIME2(3)   NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_dim_policy PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (policy_sk)
);

CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX ix_dim_policy_policy_id ON dw.dim_policy (policy_id, is_current);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_policy
    @SnapshotDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name     VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_policy',
            @rows         INT,
            @closed       INT,
            @last_loaded  DATE,
            @err_msg      NVARCHAR(4000),
            @err_no       INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';

        /* Oldest snapshot first: loading an older snapshot after a newer one
           would reopen versions that are already closed (INC-2105) */
        SELECT  @last_loaded = MAX(d.source_snapshot_date)
        FROM    dw.dim_policy d;

        IF @SnapshotDate < @last_loaded
            THROW 50001, 'dw.dim_policy already holds a later policy snapshot', 1;

        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#src') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #src;

        /* 1. This snapshot's policies with product, broker and customer segment */
        SELECT  p.policy_id,
                p.policy_number,
                p.customer_id,
                c.segment_code                          AS customer_segment,
                pr.product_code,
                pr.product_name,
                pr.lob_code,
                ISNULL(p.broker_code, 'DIRECT-SALES')   AS broker_code,
                b.broker_name,
                p.status,
                p.inception_date,
                p.expiry_date,
                p.cancellation_date,
                p.annual_premium,
                p.currency,
                p.vehicle_reg,
                p.ncd_years
        INTO    #src
        FROM    stg.policy_snapshots p WITH (NOLOCK)
        JOIN    stg.products pr WITH (NOLOCK)
                ON pr.product_code = p.product_code
        LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON b.broker_code = p.broker_code
        LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer c WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
        WHERE   p.snapshot_date = @SnapshotDate;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'policy snapshot', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        IF @rows = 0
            THROW 50002, 'No policies found for this snapshot date', 1;

        CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX ix_src_policy_id ON #src (policy_id);

        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        /* 2. Close the current version of policies whose status, broker, premium
              or vehicle registration has changed since the last snapshot */
        MERGE dw.dim_policy AS tgt
        USING #src AS src
           ON tgt.policy_id = src.policy_id
          AND tgt.is_current = 'Y'
        WHEN MATCHED AND (   ISNULL(src.status, '')        <> ISNULL(tgt.status, '')
                          OR ISNULL(src.broker_code, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.broker_code, '')
                          OR ISNULL(src.annual_premium, 0) <> ISNULL(tgt.annual_premium, 0)
                          OR ISNULL(src.vehicle_reg, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.vehicle_reg, ''))
        THEN UPDATE
             SET    tgt.valid_to   = DATEADD(DAY, -1, @SnapshotDate),
                    tgt.is_current = 'N';

        SET @closed = @@ROWCOUNT;

        /* 3. Open a current version for new policies and for those closed above */
        INSERT INTO dw.dim_policy
               (policy_id, policy_number, customer_id, customer_segment, product_code,
                product_name, lob_code, broker_code, broker_name, status, inception_date,
                expiry_date, cancellation_date, annual_premium, currency, vehicle_reg,
                ncd_years, valid_from, valid_to, is_current, source_snapshot_date, load_ts)
        SELECT  s.policy_id, s.policy_number, s.customer_id, s.customer_segment, s.product_code,
                s.product_name, s.lob_code, s.broker_code, s.broker_name, s.status,
                s.inception_date, s.expiry_date, s.cancellation_date, s.annual_premium,
                s.currency, s.vehicle_reg, s.ncd_years,
                @SnapshotDate,
                '9999-12-31',
                'Y',
                @SnapshotDate,
                SYSDATETIME()
        FROM    #src s
        WHERE   NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
                            FROM   dw.dim_policy d
                            WHERE  d.policy_id = s.policy_id
                              AND  d.is_current = 'Y')
        ORDER BY s.policy_id;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions closed', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @closed;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions opened', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;

        SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
             @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
GO

request.system_prompt:
Translate one legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) job to PySpark 4.2. Your output must reproduce the legacy output EXACTLY, record for record and value for value, bugs included: reconciliation compares every row and column with the legacy engine's own output.

Write one Python module:
- Imports only from pyspark (pyspark.sql, pyspark.sql.functions as F, pyspark.sql.types as T, pyspark.sql.Window), datetime, decimal, math, re, functools and typing.
- Exactly this entry point: def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
- inputs holds every input table by its legacy name in lower case (e.g. "stg.claims"); params holds the parameters as text (e.g. params["AsOfDate"] == "2025-12-31").
- Return a dict from each output's legacy name to a DataFrame with the output's columns. The harness then casts each column to the contract type shown, as the legacy table's insert would (so a decimal(38,6) value stored into decimal(14,2) is rounded half up).
- Never do I/O or reach engine internals: no spark.read, .write, saveAsTable, spark.conf, RDDs, UDFs, .cache(), getattr, eval, open, os or sys. spark.sql, F.expr and selectExpr only with plain string literals (no f-strings).
- Use only constants that appear in the legacy code, the parameters, or a trap card's fix guidance (format patterns, collation names). Never hard-code data values.
- Reproduce every legacy behaviour exactly, including anything that looks like a bug: never fix it. Mark each line that reproduces a suspected bug with a "# LANSH-DEFECT: <what>" comment and list the bug in defects.
- Row order: Spark has none. Wherever the result depends on order (first or last row, a running value, a cursor, NODUPKEY, RETAIN, LAG), sort on the legacy ORDER BY and then _row_seq, which every source table has in its original row order.
- Spark runs with ANSI mode on: overflow and invalid casts raise errors, and a division by zero raises; use try_divide or a guard only where the legacy engine returns NULL.
- This job keeps history between batches: inputs also hold its own previous output, dw.dim_policy (empty, with the output's columns, before the first batch). Return the whole new table after this batch.

structured_output.code:
"""Job T02: dw.usp_load_dim_policy (T-SQL) migrated to PySpark.

Policy dimension with type-2 history, loaded once per policy snapshot.
Input dw.dim_policy is the previous state of the output; the whole new table
is returned.
"""
import datetime

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T  # noqa: F401


_OUT_COLS = [
    "policy_sk", "policy_id", "policy_number", "customer_id", "customer_segment",
    "product_code", "product_name", "lob_code", "broker_code", "broker_name",
    "status", "inception_date", "expiry_date", "cancellation_date",
    "annual_premium", "currency", "vehicle_reg", "ncd_years", "valid_from",
    "valid_to", "is_current", "source_snapshot_date", "load_ts",
]

_NOT_NULL_COLS = [
    "policy_id", "policy_number", "customer_id", "product_code", "product_name",
    "lob_code", "broker_code", "status", "inception_date", "expiry_date",
    "annual_premium", "currency",
]


def _key(c):
    # SQL Server default collation (case-insensitive) with trailing-space-insensitive '='
    return F.upper(F.rtrim(c))


def _ci_isnull(c):
    # ISNULL(x, '') compared under case-insensitive / trailing-space-insensitive rules
    return F.upper(F.rtrim(F.coalesce(c, F.lit(""))))


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    snap = datetime.date.fromisoformat(params["SnapshotDate"])
    snap_lit = F.lit(snap)

    dim = inputs["dw.dim_policy"]
    ps = inputs["stg.policy_snapshots"]
    pr = inputs["stg.products"]
    br = inputs["stg.brokers"]
    cu = inputs["dw.dim_customer"]

    # INC-2105: refuse a snapshot older than the last one loaded (THROW 50001)
    last_loaded = dim.agg(F.max("source_snapshot_date").alias("m")).first()["m"]
    if last_loaded is not None and snap < last_loaded:
        raise ValueError("dw.dim_policy already holds a later policy snapshot")

    # 1. #src
    p = ps.filter(F.col("snapshot_date") == snap_lit).select(
        F.col("policy_id"), F.col("policy_number"), F.col("customer_id"),
        F.col("product_code").alias("p_product_code"),
        F.col("broker_code").alias("p_broker_code"),
        F.col("status"), F.col("inception_date"), F.col("expiry_date"),
        F.col("cancellation_date"), F.col("annual_premium"), F.col("currency"),
        F.col("vehicle_reg"), F.col("ncd_years"),
        F.col("_row_seq").alias("p_row_seq"),
    )
    prd = pr.select(
        F.col("product_code").alias("pr_product_code"),
        F.col("product_name"), F.col("lob_code"),
        F.col("_row_seq").alias("pr_row_seq"),
    )
    brk = br.select(
        F.col("broker_code").alias("b_broker_code"),
        F.col("broker_name"),
        F.col("_row_seq").alias("b_row_seq"),
    )
    cus = cu.select(
        F.col("customer_id").alias("c_customer_id"),
        F.col("segment_code").alias("customer_segment"),
    )

    j = (
        p.join(prd, _key(F.col("pr_product_code")) == _key(F.col("p_product_code")), "inner")
        .join(brk, _key(F.col("b_broker_code")) == _key(F.col("p_broker_code")), "left")
        .join(cus, F.col("c_customer_id") == F.col("customer_id"), "left")
    )

    src = j.select(
        F.col("policy_id"), F.col("policy_number"), F.col("customer_id"),
        F.col("customer_segment"),
        F.col("pr_product_code").alias("product_code"),
        F.col("product_name"), F.col("lob_code"),
        # ISNULL returns the type of its first argument (VARCHAR(10)), so the
        # replacement 'DIRECT-SALES' is truncated to 10 characters.
        F.coalesce(F.col("p_broker_code"), F.substring(F.lit("DIRECT-SALES"), 1, 10)).alias("broker_code"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: ISNULL truncates 'DIRECT-SALES' to VARCHAR(10) 'DIRECT-SAL'
        F.col("broker_name"), F.col("status"), F.col("inception_date"),
        F.col("expiry_date"), F.col("cancellation_date"), F.col("annual_premium"),
        F.col("currency"), F.col("vehicle_reg"), F.col("ncd_years"),
        F.col("p_row_seq"), F.col("pr_row_seq"), F.col("b_row_seq"),
    )

    if src.limit(1).count() == 0:
        raise ValueError("No policies found for this snapshot date")

    # 2. MERGE: close current versions whose tracked attributes changed
    s_cmp = src.select(
        F.col("policy_id").alias("s_policy_id"),
        F.col("status").alias("s_status"),
        F.col("broker_code").alias("s_broker_code"),
        F.col("annual_premium").alias("s_annual_premium"),
        F.col("vehicle_reg").alias("s_vehicle_reg"),
    )
    t_cur = dim.filter(F.col("is_current") == F.lit("Y")).select(
        F.col("policy_sk"), F.col("policy_id").alias("t_policy_id"),
        F.col("status").alias("t_status"),
        F.col("broker_code").alias("t_broker_code"),
        F.col("annual_premium").alias("t_annual_premium"),
        F.col("vehicle_reg").alias("t_vehicle_reg"),
    )
    pairs = t_cur.join(s_cmp, F.col("t_policy_id") == F.col("s_policy_id"), "inner")
    changed = (
        (_ci_isnull(F.col("s_status")) != _ci_isnull(F.col("t_status")))
        | (_ci_isnull(F.col("s_broker_code")) != _ci_isnull(F.col("t_broker_code")))
        | (F.coalesce(F.col("s_annual_premium"), F.lit(0)) != F.coalesce(F.col("t_annual_premium"), F.lit(0)))
        | (_ci_isnull(F.col("s_vehicle_reg")) != _ci_isnull(F.col("t_vehicle_reg")))
    )
    closed = pairs.filter(changed)

    # MERGE raises error 8672 when one target row would be updated more than once
    multi = closed.groupBy("policy_sk").count().filter(F.col("count") > 1)
    if multi.limit(1).count() > 0:
        raise ValueError("The MERGE statement attempted to UPDATE or DELETE the same row more than once.")

    closed_sk = closed.select("policy_sk").distinct().withColumn("_closed", F.lit(True))

    upd = (
        dim.join(closed_sk, "policy_sk", "left")
        .withColumn("valid_to", F.when(F.col("_closed"), F.date_sub(snap_lit, 1)).otherwise(F.col("valid_to")))
        .withColumn("is_current", F.when(F.col("_closed"), F.lit("N")).otherwise(F.col("is_current")))
        .drop("_closed")
    )

    # 3. Open a current version for new policies and for those closed above
    cur_after = upd.filter(F.col("is_current") == F.lit("Y")).select(
        F.col("policy_id").alias("cur_policy_id")
    ).distinct()
    new_rows = src.join(cur_after, F.col("policy_id") == F.col("cur_policy_id"), "left_anti")

    # INSERT into NOT NULL columns fails the whole batch (rolled back)
    null_cond = None
    for c in _NOT_NULL_COLS:
        cond = F.col(c).isNull()
        null_cond = cond if null_cond is None else (null_cond | cond)
    if new_rows.filter(null_cond).limit(1).count() > 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot insert the value NULL into a NOT NULL column of dw.dim_policy")

    max_sk = dim.agg(F.max("policy_sk").alias("m")).first()["m"]
    base = 0 if max_sk is None else int(max_sk)

    w = Window.orderBy(
        F.col("policy_id").asc(), F.col("p_row_seq").asc(),
        F.col("pr_row_seq").asc(), F.col("b_row_seq").asc(),
    )
    ins = (
        new_rows.withColumn("policy_sk", F.row_number().over(w) + F.lit(base))
        .withColumn("valid_from", snap_lit)
        .withColumn("valid_to", F.lit(datetime.date(9999, 12, 31)))
        .withColumn("is_current", F.lit("Y"))
        .withColumn("source_snapshot_date", snap_lit)
        .withColumn("load_ts", F.localtimestamp())
    )

    schema = {f.name: f.dataType for f in dim.schema.fields}
    ins_out = ins.select([F.col(c).cast(schema[c]).alias(c) for c in _OUT_COLS])
    upd_out = upd.select([F.col(c).cast(schema[c]).alias(c) for c in _OUT_COLS])

    result = upd_out.unionByName(ins_out)
    return {"dw.dim_policy": result}

defects.intended: Store direct business as broker_code 'DIRECT-SALES' (CR-0961). The output column is VARCHAR(12) so the full value fits.
defects.title: DIRECT-SALES truncated by ISNULL
defects.what_it_does: ISNULL(p.broker_code, 'DIRECT-SALES') takes the type of p.broker_code, which is VARCHAR(10), so direct business is stored as broker_code 'DIRECT-SAL'.

structured_output.notes:
- I didn't have the trap cards, so traps_handled is empty. The text joins (product, broker) and the MERGE change test assume SQL Server's default case-insensitive collation and its rule that '=' ignores trailing spaces. The code compares with upper(rtrim(...)). If the database uses a case-sensitive collation, remove the upper().
- NULL and empty are treated as equal, as in ISNULL(...,'') and ISNULL(premium,0).
- New policy_sk values follow on from the existing max(policy_sk), or start at 1 when the table is empty. They are numbered in policy_id order, with ties broken by policy_snapshots._row_seq, then products._row_seq, then brokers._row_seq.
- If dim_customer or products has more than one row per key, the joins repeat source rows just as the legacy does. For a new policy that means several current versions.
- The code raises an error, as the legacy THROWs or fails and rolls back, when: the snapshot is older than the last one loaded; the snapshot has no rows; one current version matches more than one changed source row (MERGE error 8672); or a new version would have a NULL in a NOT NULL column.
- load_ts uses localtimestamp(), like SYSDATETIME(). It isn't deterministic and should be excluded from reconciliation.
- Policies missing from a snapshot stay current, because there is no WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE. Unchanged policies keep their old customer_segment, broker_name and product details. Both are reproduced as is and not marked as defects.
